sampling_rate.source: the Methods of Comrie et al.'s preprint (bioRxiv doi:10.1101/2024.09.23.613567, version 1, read on PubMed Central PMC11463554): positions 'interpolated and upsampled to 500 Hz'

position_span.source: the Methods of Comrie et al.'s preprint (bioRxiv doi:10.1101/2024.09.23.613567, version 1): nine 53 cm hallways meeting at 120 degrees with three-fold symmetry, which lays the track's centrelines 183.6 cm across (4 x 53 cm x cos 30 degrees); the largest span of the tracked positions must lie within 20% of it

speed_limit.source: Iriarte-Díaz 2002, J. Exp. Biol. 205:2897-2908, Table 1: Rattus runs at most 13.78 body lengths/s at a 0.190 m body length, 2.62 m/s (from Garland 1983 and Nowak 1999); times 1.5 because the tracked point is a head-mounted LED pair, which swings faster than the body, and no source read states head speed

sessions.verification: Checked by hand on 2026-11-03 against the Zenodo record, the file and the Methods of Comrie et al.'s preprint (bioRxiv doi:10.1101/2024.09.23.613567, version 1, read on PubMed Central; the Neuron article was not available to read). File: its SHA-256 is the one the record states, and its MD5 is the record's (66e71928...). Counts: 203 units and 870,018 spikes, 709,321 position samples, the numbers the record states. Time: samples every 0.002 s (500 Hz, the rate the preprint states), 1419 s on the Unix clock starting 2021-07-10, the session's date; spikes from 0.0008 s after the first sample to 0.0002 s before the last, inside the tracking. Space: the track graph has 10 nodes and 9 edges, the nine hallways the preprint describes, with edge lengths 51.7 to 57.4 cm against its 53 cm; the largest tracked span is 202.6 cm (x), 10% more than the 183.6 cm the stated layout gives between centrelines; env.to_linear with the file's linear_edge_order and 15 cm spacing reproduces the file's linear_position exactly. Unit: cm is inferred, not stated by the file: head_speed matches |step| / dt of the stored positions (correlation 0.93; medians 6.39 and 8.04 per s, a factor of 1.26). Heading: head_orientation minus the direction of movement above 10 cm/s has a circular mean of +13.1 degrees, so it is not used as headings.
